Here's what's actually happening. Your platform reports 3.9 because it counts modelled conversions on a 7-day-click window — it's incentivised to claim credit and it back-fills conversions it can't really see post-iOS. Shopify's last-click shows 1.5 because it hands all the credit to the final click and ignores the ad that created the demand weeks earlier. Both are biased, in opposite directions. The honest truth sits somewhere between 1.5 and 3.9 — and neither number alone is real.

The fix is to stop adjudicating platform ROAS as if it were gospel and anchor on a number that can't lie to you: blended CAC. Take total spend across everything (₹7.5L here) and divide by the actual count of new customers Shopify recorded in the period. That single figure — all-in cost to acquire one real customer — is what you manage to. It doesn't care which platform claims credit.

One move: compute blended CAC for the last 30 days and set your target against contribution per customer, not against either dashboard's ROAS.

Caveat: blended CAC blurs channels together, so it won't tell you which channel to cut — but it stops you over-trusting a 3.9 that isn't bankable.

an0192.user: Nutrition brand, email channel. My CTR is the problem, I'm sure of it — only 0.9%. Last 30 days: 830,000 impressions, 7,249 clicks, 77 orders, conversion rate 1.06%, AOV ₹2,250. I'm running broad-match keywords to get reach. How do I get clicks up?
an0192.assistant:
You've diagnosed the wrong metric. CTR isn't where this is failing — pour more clicks into this and you'll just spend more to sell the same nothing. Look one step further down.

You pulled 7,249 clicks from 830,000 impressions, but only 77 of those clicks turned into orders — a 1.06% conversion rate. That's the leak. People are clicking and then not buying, which means you're buying the wrong clicks, not too few. The cause is right there in your setup: broad-match keywords. Broad match maximises reach by matching loosely-related searches, so you're paying for a flood of low-intent browsers — curious, comparing, not ready to buy nutrition. High impressions, decent raw clicks, dead conversion. That's the broad-match signature.

So the lever isn't lifting CTR — it's tightening intent. Move from broad match to phrase/exact on the terms that actually convert, layer in a heavy negative-keyword list to cut the junk searches you're paying for, and stop optimising the campaign toward clicks (which rewards exactly the cheap, low-intent traffic hurting you). Optimise toward purchases. Fewer, more expensive, far more qualified clicks will beat this every time.

Caveat: 77 orders is a thin base to pick winning keywords from — pull the search-terms report to see which actual queries drove those 77, and build your tightened list from real converters rather than guessing.
